From Tokyo to Hong Kong: Fast-fashion giant Shein could see its stock market valuation reach almost $27bn (£19.8bn) when its makes its debut in Hong Kong on 1 September.

Shein said in a filing on Monday, external that it will offer nearly 280 million shares for between HK$47.60 ($6.07; £4.45) and HK$49.50 each.

At the top of the range, the share sale would raise $1.77bn (£1.3bn) for the company and give it a market valuation of $26.8bn.

But that is much lower than the $100bn it was worth in 2022, reflecting weaker sales growth and higher costs.

The long-awaited move comes after failed attempts to list in the US and London due to regulatory challenges amid scrutiny of the firm, which has its headquarters in Singapore but was founded in China.

https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cdeweewjdxno?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss
source_title: Shein aims for almost $27bn valuation in stock market debut
source_summary: The fast-fashion giant's shares are due to start trading in Hong Kong on 1 September.

Scoreboard update: An expected drop in the unemployment rate has failed to materialise, dealing a setback to Andy Burnham’s hopes of reviving Britain’s ailing economy.

Unemployment remained stuck at 4.9pc in the three months to June, while the number of payrolled employees fell by 13,000, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics.

Economists had predicted that the unemployment rate would ease to 4.8pc.

Unemployment jumped to 5.4pc in June, up from 4.6pc the previous month.

Meanwhile, vacancies dropped to 707,000 in the three months to July – the lowest level since 2021 – with a particular strain on entry-level job openings.
